# F53 — quality of smaller and MoE models against Qwen2.5-3B Q8_0 (CPU, Linux container)

Evidence for [F53](../../../findings.md). Everything here ran on a 4-core x86-64 Linux container, CPU only,
with llama.cpp at the pinned revision (`native/split/llama-revision.txt`, `4da6337767f973e2b4d0797e5b323d77d8565e4a`).
**Nothing ran on the operator's laptop or phones.** The container's CPU changed between runs (it was recycled
several times), so the generation speeds in `results/*.humaneval.json` are not comparable with one another.

## Results (`results/summary.txt`, regenerated by `tools/summ.py`)

| Model | Wikitext bits/byte | Mean KLD vs 3B Q8_0 | Same top token % | MMLU % | HellaSwag % | HumanEval raw | HumanEval chat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q8_0 (reference) | 0.740 | - | - | 39.7 | 73.5 | 32/55 (58.2%) | 24/26 on the first 26 problems; the full run was lost (`qwen3b-q8.chat.PARTIAL.he.log`) |
| Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M | 0.752 | 0.0379 | 90.1 | 40.7 | 72.0 | not run | not run |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M | 0.796 | 0.3861 | 73.8 | 37.3 | not finished | not run | not run |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M | 0.907 | 0.6181 | 67.2 | 32.3 | 54.0 | 29/55 (52.7%) | 40/55 (72.7%) |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct Q8_0 | 0.896 | 0.5896 | 68.3 | not valid | 55.0 | 32/55 (58.2%) | 40/55 (72.7%) |
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct Q4_K_M | 0.813 | - | - | 41.3 | 81.0 | 18/55 (32.7%) | 16/55 (29.1%) |
| Granite 3.1 3B-A800M-Instruct Q4_K_M | 0.826 | - | - | 36.0 | 73.5 | 0/55 (artifact, see below) | 24/55 (43.6%) |

Perplexity in `results/*.ppl.log` is per token and **not comparable across tokenizer families**; the bits/byte
column is `log2(PPL) x tokens / 200,000 bytes` using the token count in `results/<label>.tok`, an approximation.

## Setup

- **Wikitext:** the first 200,000 bytes of wikitext-2-raw `wiki.test.raw`, `-c 512 --chunks 60`.
- **MMLU:** 300 tasks from `mmlu-validation.bin`, `llama-perplexity --multiple-choice`, zero-shot likelihood scoring.
  Absolute numbers are far below published MMLU (3B: 39.7 here against about 65 published) because of that scoring
  method; compare models with each other only.
- **HellaSwag:** 200 tasks, `llama-perplexity --hellaswag`.
- **HumanEval:** every third problem (55 of 164), greedy, pass@1, `tools/humaneval.py` (raw completion with stop
  sequences) and `tools/humaneval_chat.py` (the model's own chat template through `llama-server --jinja`).
- **Noise:** about ±2.8 points on MMLU, ±3 on HellaSwag and ±6.7 on HumanEval (n = 55).
- **Data sources:** `huggingface.co/datasets/ggml-org/ci` (wikitext-2-raw-v1.zip),
  `huggingface.co/datasets/ikawrakow/validation-datasets-for-llama.cpp` (`mmlu-validation.bin`),
  `raw.githubusercontent.com/klosax/hellaswag_text_data` (`hellaswag_val_full.txt`),
  `raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/human-eval` (`HumanEval.jsonl.gz`).
- **Models:** Hugging Face GGUF files. The Coder Q8_0 (`507de59046601282ba768a9789900e6ccf60ed93ddf346730b7c68eb0715bc47`)
  and 3B Q4_K_M (`626b4a6678b86442240e33df819e00132d3ba7dddfe1cdc4fbb18e0a9615c62d`) checksums match Hugging Face's.

## What went wrong and what it means

- **Coder Q8_0 produced `????` on the first build.** That build used `-march=native`, tuned to the container's
  CPU at build time. Builds with explicit AVX2, explicit AVX512+VNNI and no AVX at all all generate correct code from the same
  file, and the native build later failed with "Illegal instruction" on a different host. The exact instruction path was not isolated.
  Consequences: the Coder Q8_0 raw HumanEval score here comes from the AVX512+VNNI build and its MMLU result was discarded. The native build
  also produced the 3B Q8_0 reference (perplexity, MMLU, HellaSwag, raw HumanEval and the saved `ref.kld` logits), the Coder Q4_K_M perplexity, MMLU, HellaSwag and raw
  HumanEval, and the Coder Q8_0 perplexity and HellaSwag, on the earlier host where it generated sane text; the 3B Q4_K_M, 1.5B, OLMoE and Granite
  evaluations and every chat-template run used the AVX512+VNNI build. The two builds were not compared on the same file apart from the Coder Q8_0 check, so the
  KL divergences compare AVX512 runs against logits saved by the native build.
- **Granite scored 0/55 on the raw prompt** because it starts a new function right after the docstring and the stop
  sequence `\ndef ` cuts it off. That is a prompt-format artifact; with the chat template it scored 24/55.
- **ARC-Challenge was dropped.** The first runs failed (`-np 5` needed, then a large batch ran out of memory), and no valid result exists.
- **The 3B Q8_0 chat HumanEval is incomplete** (24 of the first 26 problems passed) because the container was recycled mid-run.

## Reproduce

Build llama.cpp at the pinned revision with an explicit instruction set (not `-march=native`), put the GGUF files and datasets
under one directory (`QLAB`), then:

```bash
export QLAB=/path/to/dir LLAMA_BIN=/path/to/llama.cpp/build/bin
tools/run_eval.sh qwen3b-q8 $QLAB/models/qwen3b-q8.gguf base      # saves $QLAB/out/ref.kld (4.6 GB)
tools/run_eval.sh qwen3b-q4km $QLAB/models/qwen3b-q4km.gguf vs    # KL divergence against that reference
python3 -I tools/humaneval_chat.py coder15b-q4km $QLAB/models/coder15b-q4km.gguf 3
python3 -I tools/summ.py results
```

`run_eval.sh` expects `data/wikitext-2-raw/`, `data/mmlu.bin`, `data/hellaswag.txt` and `data/HumanEval.jsonl` under `QLAB`
(HumanEval problems are executed with `python3 -I` under CPU and memory limits; run it only in a throwaway environment).
